One or two simultaneous players can tackle this marble madness-esque platformer. In Dreams anything can happen, even colored bubbles, normally calm and harmless turning in to sticky globes that wander around swallowing poor Andrea's toys. Out of breath and sweaty, Andrea wakes up and discovers that it was just a bad dream. But this bad dream gave him an idea for the next one, which begins on his next rest! Now he is dreaming of a whole world of new toys, which he has never been able to have and it is he who guides the bubbles towards th toys to wrap them and bring them to him. But there is another bubble that appears and tries to steal the toys. This game can be especially fun if played by two friends at the same time, which whips the game to a frenzied pace. There is a small red square on the route which will randomly rearrange things to be recovered, adding to the fun. 

Published as Bollicine in Italy in Top PlayGames n.22 (giugno 1987).

188212.overview: Born in the U.S.A. is a U.S. heography game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Michael Barnard and published by Softdisk Publishing, Inc. in Loadstar #32.

188221.overview: Börsenmakler 90 (translates to Stockbroker 90) is a German language turn-based (up to six players) text-based stock market simulation for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Kudi-Soft and released into the public domain in 1990.

188227.overview: Released as part of Videogiochi Settimanale #01, the game is a pretty good SEUCK shooter, Satyrigame style, where the object is to dismantle a criminal organization dedicated to the sale of alcohol in the USA in the Prohibition era.

188496.overview: Battle Throne is somewhat a tribute to Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior. It was developed and published in 2007 by Cache64.com as part of 2007's Game Over(view) Freestyle Jam

188533.overview:
Bagger is a clone of the arcade classic Tapper. The main difference being that instead of Root Beer or beer, your character is a bag boy in a grocery store.

This game was developed by Kevin Black and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/07 (Issue #61)

190648.overview:
A baccarat casion\card game published in CPU (Computer Programmert Zur Unterhaltung) 1984/02.

The game was translated to Dutch (without permission) and released by Courbois Software in the same year on Courbois Software #6426.

192404.overview:
Inspired by Lobo's cat Gelsomina, with a little Sokoban and a tiny dash of Angry Birds thrown in for flavour, Boxymoxy is a game about moving cats and smashing skulls using the power of logic. 

The stupid old Wizard had cast a wrong spell, creating an invasion of chattering skulls and now no one can sleep! Two cats, Boxy and Moxy, are set to clean up this mess. Using their combined powers, you will traverse 60 levels over three areas in order to destroy all skulls and restore the beauty sleep to the people of the old Kingdom! 

Featuring 60 challenging puzzles, unique gameplay, a player performance-graded progress system with on-cartridge saving, 15 digitally-sampled and distinct meows from 12 cats and full PAL/NTSC compatibility.

192578.overview: Blackjack 21 is a public domain single-player computerized version of Blackjack/21 for the C64. This was was developed by Donnie Russell II. The year of release is unknown,

192581.overview: Blackjack 64 is a blackjack game for the C64. It was developed by Ed Cotta and released in 1982.

192667.overview: Created using the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit, this cross-hairs shooter game was created by New Edition and Anthrax (Günther). It contains graphics that may be found offensive.

193634.overview:
Brick Battle is a Breakout clone with three different modes of play. 

-   Mode one is Single Buster, which is your standard Breakout.

-   Mode two is Double Buster in which the bricks are both on the top and bottom of the screen, however, you can still lose lives if you don't hit a brick within a certain period of time in this mode

- Mode Three is Diamond Buster in which there are bricks in all four corners of the screen. You can also lose lives in this mode if you don't hit a brick within a certain time period as well.

This game was released by Street Games as part of their "C64/128 Battle Pack" compilation.

194479.overview: Hearing the SPLAT as the small furry ball hit the ground, the ants darted under the gap at the bottom of the door and out of the small wooden hut. Then thoroughly believing that Balrog had really dropped one *this* time, the seized the small furry ball and scampered in the direction of the thick thorn hedge and comparative safety. Unknown to Balrog, the events that were soon to follow were to have a profound effect on not only his mind, but on parts of him that not even Hunniken could reach! Would he be able to free himself from his sticky predicament or would it take more pain than he could endure?

194571.overview: Animated tank battle. You program the moves of your tank ahead of time, when it will move and when it will turn and fire. Then you release all your instructions. If none of the enemy tanks shoot you, you can do another set until all the enemy tanks are gone. Released as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack".

195530.overview: An airplane flies across the screen above a city with skyscrapers. When the plane reaches the far end of the screen, it reappears on the other end, but at a lower altitude since it is running out of fuel. The objective is to drop bombs on the city to destroy all buildings so that the plane may land on level ground.

195694.overview:
Play the game that dates back to the seventeen hundreds! Move the stones across the computer board game before your opponent has the chance to do the same. A win is just a 'stones' throw away!

A game of "The Big 100" collection.

195756.overview: One bizarre Bubble Bobble rip-off where you knock your enemies about by shouting something in Swedish in their ears. Not much to this really, probably created as a joke.

195785.overview: A single screen platformer where you avoid the crawling aliens and gather all the diamonds.

195865.overview: Battle Khaos II is a multiplayer RPG game inspired by games like Magic: The Gathering, Dark Legions and Chaos – The Battle of Wizards.

195886.overview:
A SEUCK based shooter for 1 or 2 players, including simultaneous cooperative play. Released in Digital Marketing PD #092, released as Super Ball by Editions Fermont in Italy in Go Games n.43 (maggio 1989).  
 
With this beautiful arcade style game you can display your ability to control the Super Ball which you use to destroy the various asteroids and the many enemies that you will find along your path.

195887.overview: You start in a maze filled with enemies who can shoot through walls, avoid their shots and take them out. This appears to have been made with Mastertronic's Games Creator.

195891.overview: A Horizontally scrolling shooter created by Lee Hudson & David Green and presented by Break Point.

195926.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter for one or two players created by Duncan MacDonald and Dave Edwardson with music by Rob Hubbard in 1987. The game was never officially published or released.

195927.overview: A SEUCK based space Shoot'em Up created by Stuart Douglas. The Grixlons have taken over the universe and the house down the street so that there will be ETERNAL WAR! Your job is to destroy all the power orbs to destroy the Grixlons.

195928.overview: Your mission is to advance through the enemy lines, seeking for their secret headquarters and in the end, destroy it. A SEUCK created shooter created by Mikael Sundvill in 1992.

195965.overview: A pretty decent vertically scrolling shooter created with the SEUCK engine by The Lyon. For one-player or two-player simultaneous cooperative play.

195966.overview: A vertically scrolling shooter for single play or simultaneous cooperative play created with Chris Yates' SEUCK game engine and created by The Lyon in 1989.

195967.overview: A Polish-language horizontally scrolling shooter originally created with SEUCK and published by FanCA & Indy Software.

195968.overview: Blue Diamonds is a Boulder Dash game made by Boulderwilli using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit in 1989.

196037.overview: A a one player cute-em-up game created with the SEUCK engine with some interesting game sections including some interesting bosses, a section reminiscent of Freeway or Frogger and a good amount of fun from such bizarre SEUCK stuff.

196038.overview: A cute'em up also known as Radclifes Revenge and sequel to the original Bluey Blob created with the SEUCK engine and released by Bedroom Software in 1994.

196057.overview: The Evil Dr. Dactor has kidnapped the the king and his evil men have taken over a beautiful and once peaceful land. The inhabitants run and hide but out of the dark comes a hero who will save this land. His name is Bogue.

196058.overview: Boulder Dash Sab is a Boulder Dash game developed with Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit featuring 20 new caves to test yourself against. It was developed by Jason Sabourin. The year of release is not currently known and this is Jason's only known Boulder Dash game creation.

196060.overview: A game created with the SEUCK engine by Keith Killilea aka Knightcoder in 1997. He's Back! The coolest grape in the world! The evil Dactor has kidnapped all of your friends and he is going to turn them into evil ROBOTS! You must save them!

196125.overview: An early take on BomberMan on the C64, created with the SEUCK engine and published by Champion Software for one player or two-player simultaneous play. Champion Software would later revisit this game theme in "Bomberman II: Penuts" in 1995.

196167.overview: A shooter created with the SEUCK engine and published in Commodore Zone Issue #01 (September 1995). This is the follow-up to Border War. This time you are free to move around the whole screen, rather than being restricted to just one half of the playing area. You have 8 direction shooting and a weapon that spawns a wall of fire from the left and right sides of your ship.

196213.overview: Oddly, the first in the string of Bounty Hunter games, unless the first was lost to time. This SEUCK based shooter was released some time in the very early 90's by Champion Software. You must wend you way through the heavily defended fortress, destroying the guardian troops and bots before they get you. Will you be able to get your bounty? It will take a LOT of killing but.... this is the way.

196219.overview: A series of games featuring the titular bounty hunter, shooting his way multi-directionally through an enemy stronghold. You must fight many defenders and bosses to get to the end of this one.

196241.overview: Another game in the Bounty Hunter series this time with somewhat improved graphics, more types of enemies and a bit more challenge. But everything does look startlingly similar to earlier games in the series. That, along with a lack of understanding in how Roman numerals work make this a bit of a lackluster release. That said, if you enjoyed the previous parts of the collection enough is the same that you will likely enjoy this one.

196247.overview: The second to last game (thus far) in the Bounty Hunter game series created by Nik Townes for Champion Software using the SEUCK engine. You make your way to an ever increasingly well defended fortress, fighting threats from all periods of time including the distant past and the far-flung future.

196248.overview: One in a series of SEUCK games made by Nik Townes and Wil Smith (not that one) with the SEUCK engine for Champion Software in 1996. In them you are a bounty hunter making your way through a fortress defended by warriors from multiple time zones.

196348.overview: A strange and amusing Breakout variant. The Earth is being invaded by hostile creatures from outer space. The creatures are protected by a force field. Your mission is to break into the area behind the force field, and to destroy the creatures with deadly power dots. When your power dot hits the force field it will bounce back. You must use your deflector paddle to bounce the power dot back towards the creatures. Once you have destroyed the creatures, you will proceed to the next level, in which the creatures will advance faster!

196466.overview: A shooter for one or two cooperative simultaneous players created with the SEUCK engine and made by Ron Marshall aka Met.

196467.overview: The third and last in the Brothers in Arms shooter trilogy, created with the SEUCK engine by Ron Marshall aka Met.

196652.overview: Bagels is a mastermind game where the player must guess the computer's code and the computer will try to guess the player's code at the same time. Codes are four characters long and consist of the letters A through F in any order and duplication. After each guess of the computer the player must answer how many of the letters are exact (on the right position) and matches (in the code, but on a different position). The computer does the same for the player's guesses. Whoever guesses the code first wins. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1992/02-03.

196745.overview: With a whopping maximum of 999 players, This  text-based bowling game simply titled "Bowl" was developed by Paul Peraino and published by Creative Computing as a type-in in their book  "BASIC Computer Games - Microcomputer Edition"

196900.overview: BrainWave is a free puzzle game inspired by Mahjong tile removal games, the main difference being the setting and the design of the pieces. it was released in Italy under several names including Double Box, Pezzo Doppio and Piramix.

196952.overview: Use a joystick to change the colour of the borders and let the notes of the correct colour reach the border and they will highlight correctly. The game was written for the 2005 mini game compo as part of the 4K category. The game was also published in GO64! 2005/11.

197255.overview:
Welcome to the C64 casino. It is time to play some friendly Black Jack. It is double or BUST. You will be dealt a couple of cards. It will be up to you to decide whether to twist or stick to the current cards. Be careful to NOT go over 21, otherwise you'll lose some money. If however, you decide to stick. It will be up to the dealer to take another card. If over 21, you win the prize money.

Blackjack aka Twenty-One (yes that is the official name) is a 1-2 player Blackjack game developed and released into the public domain in 2014 by German programmer Jörg Heyltjes.

197257.overview: Boxxy is a 3D platformer with some similarities to games like Q*Bert. It was developed by Sean Huxter and released into the public domain in 1985.

197285.overview:
B-Raid! is a vertical scrolling shooter for 1 or 2 players (co-op) developed by Al Dukes using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was published by Argus Specialist Publications Ltd. in the following:

-     Commodore Disk User 1989/11
-     Your Commodore 1991/07 (Tape #19)

197334.overview: Not to be confused with the Amiga/Atari ST game of the same name, this game is a vertically scrolling shooter for 1-2 players (co-op) developed by Weird Scientists using SEUCK. It was published in Magic Disk 64 1988/09 and in Italy as Battle X in Byte Games n.24 (ottobre 1988).

197404.overview: It was a cold Autumn morning, but the 'gurgling' in Balrog's stomach had become very nearly unbearable and he knew that unless he paid  visit to the small wooden hut at the bottom of the garden there would soon be more in his pajamas than just him!! So slipping on his boots and picking up a copy of the Goblin Gazzette, he made his way down the path towards the waiting door. Just then a small thought flitted across his mind but he dismissed it lightly and thought to himself... "The little sods can lock the door if they want, as long as I can park my bum on the throne first!! Would everything come out all right? Or would shorts need to be shed!

197480.overview: Baji is a German language strategical board game for 1-2 players. It was developed by Boris Kocjan and released into the public domain in 1986

197950.overview: BoxWorld, the sequel to MazezaM, is a puzzle game where the player have to rearrange boxes in each level in order to be able to teleport to the next level. The game is based on the classic Soko-Ban genre with a twist: new types of boxes and terrains. The latest version includes more than 525 puzzles.

198719.overview: A single screen platformer created by Christian Degrelle and published in the French magazine Hebdogiciel N°116 (03.01.1986). You are an innocent baby gorilla, caught in the jungle by the infamous Count Serusta. The count has promised release in exchange for gathering up the scatter pieces from his gloomy dungeon.

198725.overview: A French version of the classic board game published in Hebdogiciel Software N°1. Two people play backgammon. This time, your computer is your partner.

198729.overview: A crosshairs shooter created by Arnaud Hervas and published in Hebdogiciel N°146-149 (01.08.1986) where you must hit the skeet\trap shooting disks and the balloons. The speed and amount of items being thrown out increases as you qualify for the round and move on to the next one. At level 3 some of the ballloons come straight up from behind the mountains or travel quickly from top to bottom, making your shots much more difficult. Your crosshairs will loop from the top and bottom of the screen to the other side if that helps.

198813.overview:
No to be confused with the ZX Spectrum game of the same name, this game is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by C.P. and J.J. Gosoen using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.  It was released into the public domain in 1988. In Italy, it was released under the name Bruffer in Special C64 n.4 (1991/1992) and as Cingo in Special Program n.92 (dicembre 1992). 
 
ON the moon of Cingo 12 of the XMT 125484 galaxy, the longest and most horrible war in recorded history is taking place. You are a solider of the Green army and with your tracked vehicle you are able to venture inside enemy lines to destroy as many of the enemy as possible. Use your protonic cannon and avoid as many enemy shots as you can. Beware, their goal is to annihilate you!

199272.overview: Bastion is a space shooter similar to the old vector based arcade game Star Castle. It is for 1 or 2 players (simultaneous co-op).  Bastion is a futuristic, one- or two-player arcade-style shoot-'em-up in which your spaceship tries to blast its way through layers of rotating shields. It was developed by Steve Harter and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1990/11.

199344.overview: In Blindganger you play a blind person who is stuck in a sewer system. You have to find the exit by listening to the environment sounds. "Ssshh" stands for no obstacle, "Kunk" for sewer wall, "Beep" for deep well and "Tink" for the exit. Every couple of minutes, a wave flushes you through the sewer and you have to make your way back. When the time expires or you make it to the exit, an overview of the map is shown. Blindganger was published in the dutch magazine "Commodore Dossier" issue 17 in 1988. It was written in BASIC with some assembler routines.

199345.overview:
"Number 2043: You are imprisoned in one of the best prisons ever conceived. Any attempt at escape would be useless. that is why you must remain calm and understanding.

(Circular for prisoners): You who, like us, are here, we advise you to run away from the walls that block your way with your cannonball as well as with your joystick connected to the port1 this one will give you freedom. Unfortunately the builders are smart and as you progress the walls will thicken. More at a time the bricks will move making the task difficult but do not weaken !!!! (The prisoners' committee)"

199523.overview: Nothing like a good game of Belote against his machine to relax after all the space battles and other warlike entertainment. This is a gambling game played with a 32 card deck. Published in Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and Hebdogiciel Software N°5.

200184.overview: Boulder Dash Senior was developed by Andreas "Holy Moses" Kwias using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit. It was a follow up to his first two "Boulder Dash Junior" games.

200412.overview:
A very simple shooter game where you navigate the sky in a hot air balloon and drop bombs on enemy tanks down below. The  game was first published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/08 (Issue #14), and also in Courbois Software #6431. It was released in Australia and New Zealand as part of "Red Pack" compilation. Floating along in your hot-air balloon is a nice way to spend a beautiful summer morning. But you've got a mission; To destroy the enemy's tanks, which are threatening your force's flank. 
 

Alone in your anti-tank hot-air balloon, you're drifting along and enjoying the tranquility of a beautiful summer morning. And hoping the enemy stays out of sight — but you know they won't. They're sending their best tanks (which are wily and evasive) to get to your troop's southern flank, and your job is to destroy them. If you're skillful enough to stop the first wave, you're ready for the next game level. There are 6 difficulty levels with 6 as the most difficult.

200629.overview:
Released by Funsoft as Time Runner in North America and by WizardSoft as Blade Runner in Italy, this Amidar style action game was created by Scott Maxwell & Troy Lyndon. 

Time Runner is a game in which you move your character along a pellet grid, which changes from level to level, while you collect points and avoid enemy characters. The goal is to, similar to PacMan, cover the entire board and fill-in each rectangular area, which will then become colored in. Time Runner was first developed on the Atari 800 and later converted to the Commodore-64.

200640.overview:
Spirit of Ben Hur (also known as Ben Hur Challenge and Ben Hur) is a solitaire card game developed by Knees Calhoon and G.F. Collins. It was published in Loadstar #169 in 1998.

Rules/gameplay:

There are two goals to the game: try to build UP the foundations by suit from the ace to the king; and
try to do it with as few spins of the tableau as Possible.

The aces are removed from the deck and placed in the "Colosseum area" forming the four foundations. Then fourteen cards are dealt around the foundations The rest of the cards are placed face down and turned one at a time to a Single waste Pile.

The top card of the waste pile is available for play to the tableau or the foundations. Cards in the tableau Can be played to the foundation only if they are in the same row or the same column as
the foundation Pile.

There is no building in the tableau. Empty spaces in the tableau may be filled from the waste Pile only.
The game is won if all cards are built to the foundation.

The game can be played with either a joystick or a mouse.

200818.overview:
An exciting new action adventure game for your Commodore 64! Travel back to the days of yore and do battle in a kingdom besieged by mighty dragons and other dark forces. 
 
Can Sir Bob help the hapless townspeople who's normally tranquil kingdom has been overrun by evil wraiths, undead souls, savage beasts and evil dragons!
Your quest is to explore the kingdom, enter buildings, dispatch the evil minions that lurk inside and then you will be rewarded either with an item of treasure, arrows to boost your ammo or a piece of the Master Sword.
Once you have all the Master Sword pieces you will be able to enter the castle and do battle with the dragon. If you manage to dispatch this fiend then you will rescue the princess!

202001.overview:
An unofficial entry in the Great Giana Sisters franchise, this game was created out of whole cloth by Von Laserdance of Rush using the Shoot'em-up Construction Kit and was released in SYS PD Diskett#45 (1993) and actually published in Italy under several names, including Baby Crazy in Nova Games n.24 (Ottobre 1988).  
 
It isn't a stellar outing for Laserdance as this lacks all the platforming elements beloved in this game and sticks to just the Shooter and collect-em up components.

This is not a typical platform game like Giana, it's actually a SEUCK game in disguise.

202128.overview:
Basket Case is a "catch it" style in game in which you have to catch apples falling from trees in a basket. 

This was developed by J. Latimer and published in ReRun 1990/08-09-10.

202163.overview:
A 2 player only vs shooting game in which you have to shoot BBs/pellets at the other player. Like in the majority of these games, the winner is determined after so many rounds with the player with the most victories being the eventual winner.

This was developed by William Chin and published in the following:

•   COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/08 (Issue #62)
•   Best of Gazette 1988 (Disk Issue)

It was also published in 1993 in Europe under the name Ball Barricade (with SLIGHTLY altered graphics) by Digital Talk in Digital Talk #003 (26.09.1993) which was a European based disk only magazine.

202735.overview: A SEUCK based shooter created by Timothy Agar for one or two player simultaneous play.

203381.overview:
A spaceship is on a mission: it flies over enemy bases and is subjected to fire from the base and must avoid flying objects, for impact with them can destroy your craft. The action begins in a path limited by two walls which must not be touched. you will need to be a master pilot to avoid the walls, enemy fire and craft. You have three lives to get you to the end of the challenge. 

Published in Italy as Moonbase in Logica 2000 n.90 (1989).

204512.overview: Inspired by the popular reality TV show of the same name (UK version) Big Brother Simulator is a strategy game in which you have to choose your decisions wisely to avoid eviction from the "Big Brother" house. This game was developed by Andrew Vaisey and released as part of the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2006 (C64CGC).

204776.overview:
Hello boils and ghouls...

This is Beatnik Bert. Man, my pipe is haunted, ya dig? I gotta skip down to da basement and try to get it lickety split before i miss my gig at Scoody's Playhaus. But I'm a Scaredycat, dig?? There's all sort of creepy shadows da'n there! Watch out for my bongos! They have gone just mad man! OH.. No jive, watchout for those haunted ashes too.

205374.overview: The Black Jewel is a text adventure game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Frank McMahon and released into the public domain in 1986. Along with his other titles, this "Real Frank" game was distributed via the QuantumLink "Q-Link" Commodore dial-up "online" service, operated by Quantum Computer Services which later became AOL.

205404.overview:
The objective of this 2015 SEUCK game created by Roberto Ricioppo is simple...

Fly back to your home planet of Ziridium. Unfortunately your trip back home to Ziridium won't be that easy, as you will be facing battles against the alien forces. 

Can you fight down the aliens and reach home, or will your ship be destroyed so badly, the workers on board won't be able to restore it?

205405.overview: Based on one of Jim Butterfield's ML games for the KIM-1. The computer randomly chooses 4 letters, between A - F. You must type in the four letters in order to guess the hidden code. The computer will show a number in two columns on the right hand side. The right letter, but in the wrong place, or a number of letters that are in the correct place. These are marked as EXA and MUTE. After your complete the first code. You can work on the next one. Somewhat similar to Mastermind.

205406.overview:
You are Bergbert der Rächer (translates to Bergbert the Avenger). Wulfgar the Evil is about to conquer the World. Put on your superhero suit, charge your overkill emitter and make it to his lair. Defeat Wulfgar, so earth will be free and safe again." Instructions in particular: Kill everything that moves. Don't touch anything that moves.

Despite the game's German name, the game itself is entirely in English.

205407.overview:
This is a puzzle game, in which you move counters A, B, C around the grid, in order to prevent counter D from getting to the most bottom point. Full instructions are revealed on the scroll text.

The game is actually an unofficial update of a 1983 BASIC type-in game with improved graphics, and added sound/music.

205717.overview:
Bottle Neck is a homebrew puzzle game for the Commodore 64. You have to move the blocks, so they remove the bottle caps that are on the screen by matching the blocks to their colors. You can also match the blocks to the other blocks as well, but you only get points if they are on top of a bottle cap and remove the cap. The game is similar to Dr. Mario in that regard.

The game was developed by Michael Riley and released into the public domain in 1992.

205726.overview:
Baloon 64 (spelled Balloon 64 on the title screen) is a Spanish language miscellaneous arcade style game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Khaleel Al-Ghamdi and published b6 Sintax S.A. in the Your Computer #5 compilation cassette, which was released in 1986.

You play the character of a weird little alien space ship (or robot) and your goal is to collect all the balls from the bottom of the screen, and bring them to the empty black holes on the top, but make sure you don't hit the balloons or you will lose a life.

205772.overview:
The Tale So Far ....
There was nothing a BALROG enjoyed more than a 'green-cheese’ sandwich, especially one that had been allowed to 'ferment' for a week or two! It also helped if the cheese had been laid to rest between two thick slices of good brown bread 

... BALROGS have been known to go to war over such delights. However, unbeknownst to this particular Balrog, such joys were suddenly brought to a sudden end ... by a strange‘scratching’ noise at the door of his abode. This noise — would cause him to become involved with the likes of 'Lemin-Rats', cockroaches’ and nasty ‘Red-Caps", as he struggled to solve some very devious problems indeed.

Would he be able to find the means to cross the bridge, or even to assist the young boy in his search for the 'impossible'? Would he dare to venture close enough to the dark trees Vs to locate the object of his desires? Could he
attract the attention of the boat-manor, even discover the whereabouts of the runaway Donkey?

The answers to these and numerous other problems are all there, but are you clever enough and brave enough to find them ..... or will the task
simply be too much for both You and the BALROG ?

205774.overview:
Battle in the Fourth System is a side scrolling SEUCK game developed by Roberto Ricioppo in 2013 and published under Richard Bayliss' The New Dimension label.

Battle your way in the fourth system, shooting out enemy air craft which are out to destroy you. Good luck.

205821.overview: Blood War is a very green vertically scrolling helicopter themed SEUCK game for 1-2 players (co-op) developed by Ulf Tidstrand and published in SYS PD SPD-Disk #3 in 1990. The game itself was written in 1989, but not released until 1990.

205899.overview:
Burn Rubber (not to be confused with Burnin' Rubber) is a 1984 top-down racing game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jonathan Cook and released as a type-in listing in the book "COMPUTE!'s Second Book of C64 Games"

Game Description:

The objective of the game is to drive around the track as fast as possible without crashing. You can go as many laps as you like. You can race for points or for time. To end a lap or reset the clock, you must drive the car off the screen at the lower left. There is no top speed, but the faster you go, the harder it is to drive.

206268.overview: Bounty Hunter is an educational U.S. geography game developed by Daniel Aven. It was published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1987/08 (Issue #50).

206660.overview:
Initially released in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/04 (Issue #10), and then later in Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette. "Bingo 64" is a cleverly written computer version of the classic game. It makes good use of the 64's graphics and sound capabilities to provide you and three friends with many exciting games of bingo.
 
Few people have not known the anticipation, heard the click of the balls, the call of the number, and finally, the excited shout of "Bingo!" Here's a four-player version of this world-famous game written for the Commodore 64.

206661.overview:
Of all the Backgammon games for the C64, this is certainly one of them. Originally published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/11 (Issue #29), and then later in COMPUTE!'s Third Book of C64 Games. The classic game of backgammon combines equal parts of luck and strategy. This version observes all the regulations of standard backgammon. For the 64, VIC PIus/4, and C16.  
 
In this game of backgammon, you play against the computer. Using a decision-making algorithm described below, the computer figures out the best moves. You'll find it 
quite a challenge to come up with a winning strategy. The only thing missing is the doubling cube, which is sometimes used in gambling.

206679.overview: A Worm\Snake game published in COMPUTE! 1984/04 (Issue #47) and in the Street Games "Red Box" release in Australia and New Zealand. The game is featuring Nerm the Worm, who is trapped in Bemer Castle and would like nothing more than to escape (and consume a generous helping of "magic mushrooms" along the way). Yet another variation on Snake where the player controls a serpentine crawler in perpetual motion, which must be guided to consume food, dodge deadly walls, and avoid biting its own tail. The castle is composed of eleven rooms, each trickier to navigate than the last. In a vaguely Carrollian manner, the rooms are prone to sprouting mushrooms which cause Nerm to grow as he eats them: after consuming five mushrooms, the exit doors will open, leading to the next room. Extra lives are awarded along the way, presumably another effect of the magical fungi.

206915.overview: Brick Yard is a pinball game developed by Charles M. Duncan using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set. It was published as part of PCS Club Disk #20 in 1991.

206916.overview:
From the developer of Lady Pac, comes Bagman Comes Back, a game inspired by the 1982 Valadon Automation arcade classic, Bagman.

This version is made up of 8 completely new stages.

The game works perfectly on both PAL and NTSC models. However, for game speeds similar to the original arcade game, it is suggested using a NTSC C64, or an emulator running in NTSC mode.

206918.overview: BridgePro is a copmputerized version of the trick-taking card game, Bridge. It is for 1 or 2 players, and the first version was released by Computer Management Corporation in 1984. This version, however, the only version of the game available currently is the updated version 5.0 from 1986.

207202.overview:
Follow the adventures of Briley, a modern day girl lost in a strange new world...

“When Briley Forester is torn from her world and dumped into the backward village of Maepole, she discovers that being a witch is hard, and that Smokey, her grumpy talking cat, knows more about men than she does. 

Aided by an ancient grimoire, only by learning the powers of witchcraft can she ever hope to survive. 

But her journey is fraught with danger. The powerful Whitehead family, haters of witches, will stop at nothing to be rid of her. 

And lurking within the forest, the dark spirit lies in wait, ready to strike...” 

Take control of Briley as she explores her new life, aided by Smokey, her grumpy talking cat - and best friend.

207349.overview: B-Bert is a clone of Q*bert written entirely in BASIC by Simon Stelling for the 2008 edition of the 20 Zeilen BASIC Compo.

207440.overview: Barriers is an avoid-it style game in which you have to move through the walls and avoid the stationary enemy ships. It was developed by Digital Monastery (with Andrea Rosa on coding and graphics, and Richard Bayliss supplying the SFX and music) and was released into the public domain on  September 27, 2018.

207442.overview: Originally created by Joonas Lindberg of Digital Monastery as a tape loader game that you would play while waiting for your primary game to load. In this game you must smash all the bricks to complete a level. Don't let your ball fall through the bottom of the screen. Watch out for the evil paddle which whizzes by you constantly.

207522.overview: A war strategy game created by Eugen Traeger and published as part of the "64'er Lern-Spiele" sample disk which was included in 64'er 07/1993 / a.k.a. "Castle Wars".

207525.overview: Break & Enter: A Crazy Thief Game is an unreleased prototype from 2019. The game so far has only been released as a playable demo/preview.

208082.overview: Bumper Buster is a pinball game for the Commodore 64 developed by Ronald B. Rome using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Ponstruction Set. The year of released is not currently known. Was released as part of Pcs Club Disk #36.

208102.overview: Spanish language Bingo simulation developed by Rafael Munyoz Alfonso and published by SIMSA in Commodore World #07 (09/1984).

208440.overview:
Boing is a game developed and released by Richard Bayliss and graphics by his brother, Philip on Richard's TND label in 1997. One of the earliest games on the label.

The object of this game is to safely guide Blobbo across the bridge without getting crushed by a rolling barrel.

To do this, you will need to press the fire button on the joystick plugged into port #1. This will not be an easy task because you have to test your reaction skills. If you press the button too soon or too late, then you're finished.

However, if you press fire at the correct time, the player will be able to jump over the barrel and cross the bridge. You will also score a bonus of 10 points.

After the end of each stage, the barrel speeds up.

208459.overview: Created with help from the Shoot'em Up Construction Set, this game created by TheReaperUK, in it you fly the bird and destroy everything that moves. Collect power up balls for lives and weapons. The game has a pleasant Gameboy feel to it.

208460.overview: A challenging skill platformer created by Carleton Handley for the 2020 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition.

208461.overview: Released by Niclas for the Minigame Competition 2002. Guide Bob through the world by jumping on platforms. Don't fall or you'll lose energy. Get energy back by eating worms.

208478.overview: A new version of Boulder Dash Junior by Andreas Kwias (Holy Moses) and released for Pandemic level fun and learning. Intended for young and aspiring Boulder Dash players, or just the young at heart.

208481.overview: Intended for young and aspiring Boulder Dash fans and the eternally youthful, you must guide Rockford as he digs his way through the underground collecting Diamonds, while also avoiding baddies and being squashed by large heavy boulders. So yes very much like boulder dash, but featuring lots of cool new levels, a lovely loading screen, a great soundtrack, and even more ways to deal with enemies. Hold fire plus push a direction to act without moving. If you can solve all the tasks without the trainer and able to outscore Kermit then you are ready for the standard Boulder Dash games.

208482.overview: A remix release of the original Blockheads Boulder Dash game, released by the Netherlands Blockheads Distribution Company in 1987. It has a total of 20 caves to explore on 20 levels.

208501.overview: Released near December 2021with Christmas Rockford, a Jingle Bells Rave and some nice holiday effects. The exit on each level is well hidden and you just need to get one diamond, so pick an easy one. Never give up on Christmas!

208503.overview:
The evil witch Neatrix was planning to go about her business when she suddenly realized that her beloved cat Mr Skatla was missing. So she sets out to find the feline animal, but that would be a short game if the cat was quickly found.

Instead, she has to deal with an Austrian physicist and, consequently, with enchanted boxes.

208515.overview: A horizontal shooter, created by Jonathan Wells, who introduced the code for "Sideways SEUCK" shooters. Jon was a master of adding his own coded power-ups, and even added large baddies which exploded together and not in annoying chunks. It was initially released as a working preview in Commodore Format's, Powerpack #36 and was improved upon and released to the scene to continue improving. Jonathan says all his games will one day be completed and hopefully released in his own final format, until then this is a nice shooter and a fun hour or two of diversion.

208517.overview: A breakout game created in 1988 using the breakout construction kit. It appears to have been intended to be a VS breakout game, with blocks in the middle to break through and blocks behind your bat to protect on both top and bottom. When one side is broken enough to let a ball pass through it moves to the next level. However, second player support is unfinished and if you only have one joystick plugged in, it will mirror movements on the top and bottom. Since the balls start out on roughly mirrored trajectories, if you can keep the balls hitting in the very center of the bat you can mirror it for a while, but hit on the ends and the symmetry stops and chaos begins.

208518.overview: A version of BoulderDash created by Sub7 and created to be one of the hardest Boulder Dash game to finish. Despite its difficulty, it is highly rated. This Fan game was created with 20 caves on 5 levels using the original BoulderDash engine.

208571.overview: Another treat from the Belgian bombshell, called No One, for your spelunking delight. A set of 20 caves using the PLCK Boulder Dash engine created by different makers and compiled by No One with a special twist which allowed a surprise effect: Every time you play, the caves are different. Over a million different variations of play!! Originally published in 1987 and then updated and re-released in late 1988. The game was originally released in 2 parts, but eventually at least 24 were part of the Delight series.

208580.overview: Another treat from the Belgian Basehead, No One. This time another 20 caves with a randomizer that puts the levels in an unexpected order and you can change the type of foes and obstacles to delight you. Over a million combinations can be had! Originally released in 1987 and re-released on August 7, 1988. Created using the PLCK version of the Construction Kit and caves from several different (mostly Belgian) makers. Every time you play it will be different.

208581.overview: Explore caves made by others, create ones of your own. A Boulder Dash Construction Kit on steroids with support for both tape and disk. Made by Dave or was it AndyJ in 1988 to help smooth the path for new Boulder Heads to create quality fun for themselves and all their BBS friends!

208693.overview: Another BoulderDash game given to us by No One of the Replica Copy Crew with 20 new caves over 5 levels of play. Created using a version of the Boulder Dash Construction Kit and the BD1 engine.

208870.overview: Released for Halloween 2021 with some dangerous rockslide areas and lots of new caves to explore. Intended as a trainer for young children these Junior Boulder Dash games can teach the youngsters of age and heart how to become a BoulderHead. Remember, some of the things you will learn is how NOT to be greedy, get your diamonds and get to the next level.

209029.overview:
Your goal is to clear each screen of robots and then leave via one of the exits, avoiding the electrified walls. Doing so will earn you a bonus, but leaving a screen before all the robots are killed will cause you to be labelled a chicken and forfeit any bonus. As your score increases, the robots' speed and number of bullets they can fire simultaneously will also increase, indicated by their changing colour. In later levels the robots can fire at twice the speed and therefore become extremely deadly.

Take too long to clear a screen and 'Evil Otto' will appear, bouncing towards you. He cannot be destroyed so you may need to escape the screen if he gets too close and accept the verbal abuse from the robots.

A key tactic is to entice robots to shoot or walk into each other (or walls), and you can also lure Evil Otto to kill robot stragglers or any trapped in a closed-off section of the map.

While, the voice samples are a little off, this is far closer to the original arcade in terms of gameplay than 2013's Berzerk Redux is.

209343.overview:
It is a time of darkness. While the Sultan is off fighting a foreign war, his Grand Vizier Jaffar has seized the reins of power. Throughout the land, the people groan under the yoke of tyranny, and dream of better days. You are the only obstacle between Jaffar and the throne. An adventurer from a foreign land, innocent of palace intrigues, you have won the heart of the Sultan's lovely daughter. And in so doing, you have unwittingly made a powerful enemy. On Jaffar's orders, you are arrested, stripped of your sword and possessions, and thrown into the Sultan's dungeons. 
 
Prince of Persia Battle Hardened 2: Battle Hardened with Vengeance is a Custom set of level based on the original DOS Prince of Persia game. This mod continues the storyline of the 1st Battle Hardened. There is a new chief antagonist, Nazaam, with Jaffar being pushed back to be a secondary villain. This mod was originally created for the Dos version by KJ, a content creator from Malaysia, and converted to the C64 by Starwindz and released in the Prince of Persia Total Pack.

209754.overview: Bloo’s Magic Trip was a neat “Jack Attack” clone developed by Gareth Taft back in 1991, with his “Magic Trip” probably due to the magic mushrooms he has to consume no doubt!  The creator worked with Zeppelin Games for some time but the project never moved forward, in 1993, as it had not been picked up for publication, he released it as PD homebrew.

209755.overview: A German language action game created by Gerrit Knoef and published in Input 64 1987/10. The pinball rockets into the maze and you must guide it towards all the numbers or letters by controlling the gates and where they direct the ball. To win the level you must hit all the numbers or letters in order and exit the maze. In some levels you must also avoid wandering monsters.

209756.overview: A SEUCK based, fast-paced fun for two players that seems inspired by Bounder reborn as a shooter. Made in 1990 by Andrea Germi. Some spiteful sprites carried off your sweetheart, will you blast them? Avoid traps, blast the baddie and get the girl in the end!

210042.overview:
Welcome new member of the great Bugs Incorporated family.

Your first mission will be to exterminate the giant worm pests called 'Giant malum cimex' and the spiders 'Aspersos maculis aranea giant'.

Whose favorite food is the species of flowers 'Meridionali flos giant'.

Each of these insects have a subspecies that is differentiated by the color of its pigmentation. The slowest being the green ones and the fastest being the red ones.

Your main tool will be your Comm-0-do-re 64 sprayer, which will eliminate each of them effectively. If you press its button several times, the shooting cloud will rise, making it a more deadly insecticide, as well as reach places that previously seemed inaccessible. For better control of your movements, plug your joystick into port 2 of the device.

Your modern device will detect in the upper part of your display the number of eggs left for each of the separate insect variants by its pigmentation.

Armed with his sprayer, you must make each and every one of the pests disappear from the 5 greenhouses where rare plant species is being grown.

210240.overview: The last humans have fled earth and live now in a big generation space ship. It is a big ship on a long journey, so eventually some components fail that the robot mechanics can't fix. Now it is your turn, cadet Samuel Fox, to solve the problems and to talk to the inhabitants of the ship which are... a rather unusal combination of people.

210328.overview: Bug Hunt is a game in which you play a little reptilian creature who loves catching insects with his tongue to consume. Avoid the wasps though, as they can cause loss of life. Developed for the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2015/2016.

210373.overview:
A short entry for a title that was started back in 2006 and which was highlighted to us recently by Ken Knight.

The game is a decent looking platformer, with a few bits of graphics borrowed from Mayhem In Monsterland at this early stage. It’s not too bad, but unfortunately it seems after this proof of concept, interest was lost.

The preview was released at the Evoke 2006 party in Germany, where it won 2nd place in the Wild Demo competition. Could it some day be completed or has been put to rest for good?

Developer Stefan Mader is still active on the C64 scene, having made 2019’s Slipstream game for Psytronik Software.

210374.overview:
It’s always a shame when you come across a title which is still fairly recent, but seems to have just been left by the wayside.

Brickout is one such game, which when released back in 2007 in its preview form, won a lot of fans for whoever played it. It was a great conversion of a popular Android/PC game.

Overall it looks pretty complete, and not really needing a huge amount to finish it all off. Just what happened to the game and will it ever be finished?

We hope to find out from the developers very soon!

210375.overview:
Brainway is a simple puzzler, very similar to titles such as Sensitive, but where you must destroy all the tiles with purple circles on and without getting stuck or falling.

It’s a nice twist on games like Sensitive, and was actually due for release by Genias in 1990.

For reasons unknown, it was abandoned, even though it was fully completed. We hope to speak to the developers in the future to find out exactly what happened.

210405.overview: Battle is a 1987 fixed screen shooter in which the player controls a green tank at the bottom of the screen and must shoot down enemy helicopters as they cross the screen. The game was developed by a coder only known as Erik, and published in Joystick 03.

210581.overview: A SEUCK based shooter for one or two player simultaneous play created by Asif Bhagwandin and published in Commodore Force #06 (June 1993) - Reel Action #12

210585.overview: Released by Blazon on 16 Nov 2018 for the Intro Creation Competition 2018, this is an intro to another game that has a playable game while your main game is loading. In this one you navigate the difficult cave environment and try not to touch the stalagmites or stalactites.

210657.overview: A multi-genre on game where each screen is something different. The first level is straight action, avoid the bouncing blocks to get the key and escape, the second is a skill platformer where you need to jump from platform to platform to get to your rocket. The third is an avoid it level where you must avoid the asteroids to make it to the next planet, the next is lunar lander style landing of your ship, then a mini puzzle game, where you need to match the movements on 2 sections of blocks, then a space navigation challenge, then on to another simple platformer. Lot of mini games fun from Michael Ware and published in Commodore Disk User 1989/03-04 and also in Your Commodore 1991/02 (Tape #14)

210688.overview: Balloon Flight is a 2018 public domain game for the C64. Guide your hot air balloon through the sky while avoiding stars and walls. The game was developed by Stefan Kostic and originally released in 2018. An updated version was released in 2021, however.

210689.overview: Black Lightning is a C64 vertically scrolling SEUCK game. It was developed by Paul Ceupoens (also known as The Lyon) and released into the public domain in 1988.

210786.overview: Bob is a public domain German language bobsledding game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Ludger Dinkelbach and came out in 1984. The game has up to 10 players alternating turns.

211315.overview:
Bad Moon Rising (C64)

A European expedition makes a very unexpected discovery - a secret hidden German base ... ON THE MOON!! Can you help the hapless European Space Agency astronauts evade capture in this multi-level disk-only game for the C64?

You must survive the torture screen, negotiate the German factory in your captured ship, blast your way through an Operation Wolf inspired level, escape through the shaft, battle over the surface of the moon in a beautifully parallaxed scrolling shoot 'em up level and then punch and kick your way through the final beat'em up level.

The game was initially PAL only, but NTSC support was added shortly after the first batch was sold.

212763.overview:
Deep down in the dark and gloomy dungeons of the Spike Empire, an innocent bouncy ball has been held in captivity, chained to…. a ball, a heavy iron ball that is!

Ball and Chain is an endless runner where the difficulty ramps up until you inevitably “drop the ball.”

One day, after a generous helping of helium (no idea where he found it), our hero decides to flee the Spike Empire and return to the land of fun and games.

You control the helium filled hero and while the iron ball limits your movement, it can also be used as a weapon! Your escape for freedom comes to an end when you either collide with an enemy, or are crushed by a wall. Pressing the fire button shortens the chain and gives tighter control over the iron ball, releasing the button pushes the iron ball to the opposite direction.
The score increases the longer you stay alive. Collect coins and stars along the way to increase your score further. Stars improve the time base scoring factor, but come at a cost. They also increase the mass of the iron ball, thus increasing its weight and inertia until you are unable to spin it or even lift it from the ground.

212799.overview: A short program by Patricia Grady and published in the book "St. Michael Computer Games Micromasters" in 1984. This is game, but a game created to help student programmers realized more thoroughly how to use graphics with keyboard characters with color codes and patterns that might allow you to make a simple ship or a more complex PETSCII portrait. How colors and backgrounds impact them and how to group repeating characters to make a design. It is an 11 line treatise on making mountains out of molehills and making art from simple keystrokes.

212800.overview:
Sequel to the game Block'N'Bubble with 20 new challenging, tricky levels and new new graphics of Andreas Bauernfeind. It is a game where you have to trap all the bubbles without touching them. It features 2 player simultaneous play. 

It should be noted that the levels are extremely difficult to master!

213129.overview: Brick It is a single player Breakout clone for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Eddy Lorenzon and published by Tergeste Software (Tergestsoft), which was his own label in 1986. The game is keyboard controlled only.

213283.overview:
Buckle up, beat the beasts, and... bring back my bones!

In this swift shoot-n-collect pseudo 3D game, you are to bring together the scattered bones of your crazy uncle. He may have left you a hefty sum... but you won't know it until you talk to his ghost, stuck in between worlds.

So venture into the dark forest to gather all his bones. Watch out though - it's no mushroom picking.

His earthly remains are closely guarded by some seriously scary soul-devouring beasts. Once you've got them all, cook up some fresh broth - and hear back from your uncle!

Bones, beasts, and broth - what a craptastic story!


Controls

W - move forward

A - rotate left

S  - move back

D - rotate right

, [comma] - strafe left

. [dot] - strafe right

SPACE BAR - starts new game, shoot

P - pause
 
 
Released At :2022 C64 4kb Game Coding Competition

213329.overview: An action\party game for two players in simultaneous competitive play. One player is on the left of the screen, the other on the right. Both need to stay off the pot, this game created for the Craptastic 2022 competition gets this one right on the nose, the brown nose, that is. Jump to avoid the porcelain sitters that scream at you like Montezuma's ghost. Jump to grab the bog roll, you'll need it! The one who runs away with the most points at the end wins!

213439.overview:
Rescue the ice load of a space freighter! Beware the planet Thiera from dying of thirst! The complicated security robots must not be underestimated!

After the great interplanetary war, drinkable water has become rare. The population of Thiera will die of thirst shortly. The since long overdue arrival of the ice freighter "Baccaroo" is yearningly awaited. When contact is made with the gigantic spaceship, the crew does not answer.

What might have happened? Was the ship hijacked by pirates and was the crew eliminated? Unfortunately, this suspicion is confirmed by a surveillance probe: Ice pirates were on the ship, and they have triggered the automatic security mechanism. This protection consists of 251 ice caring robots that are moving on the 35 decks of the freighter carrying their cold load. Each of these numbered robots carries an ice block inside it and explodes at unwarranted contact.

To recover the load, a defusing manipulator is sent on its way and automatically docks at the space freighter. Due to safety reasons, the manipulator has to be remotely controlled from this point onward. You, as the best technician in the space fleet, take over this task!

Published in Happy Computer 1988/04, in 64'er Sonderheft 61, and also in 64'er Spielesammlung #4.

213490.overview: Braille is an educational program that intends to teach users how to read and write in braille (a readting/writing system for the visually impaired) it was developed by Josh Rothman & D'Arcy Nolan and published by Commodore Educational Software in 1983.

213836.overview:
Bridger is a unique strategical board game for two players only. The goal is to be the first player to successfully build a bridge on the game board.

The game was developed by David M. Moorman and published in Loadstar #238 in 2005.

213838.overview: Bridgebrain (also spelled as Bridge Brain) is a 1986 computerized implementation of the strategical card game bridge for 1 or 2 players for the Commodore 64 home computer. It was developed by George H. Bodnar and published in Loadstar #046.

214564.overview: Catch the bunny rabbits but avoid the bears in the catch it/avoid it hybrid for the Commodore 64. The Bunny Hop was developed by James C. Hilty and published in UpTime Vol.2 #09.

214851.overview:
In this game, you play a boot. Your goal is to squash as many "bugs" as possible within 2 minutes. This is a one key game. You only need to press the return (enter on modern computers) to squash the little critters.

This game was developed by Terry P. Barrett and Steve W. Colwill and published as a type-in game in the book "Winning Games on the Commodore 64 in 1984.

214876.overview: A single player homebrew logic puzzle created by Charles Grey and released in 2018.

214877.overview: A game created by István "Steveboy" Maros in 2017. A Battleships game in BASIC that is not only fun but interesting just to look at, with a unique interface for firing unlike any I've seen before but one that is instantly intuitive.

214878.overview: A golf game by Matthew Clarke aka Larcky aka Matth3w was in the Forum64 & Protovision Game Competition 2017 - Sports event. A precursor to the unfinished, upgraded Top-Hole Golf.

214879.overview: An arcade style platformer where you take Sir Percy and grab gold, coffers and time bonuses avoid the eye of the beholder! Game created by Marco Pistorio and Gaetano Chiummo of MP Software and released in 2017.

214880.overview: Similar to the original Beholder, put out that same year you must help Sir Percy grab the gold, coffers and time bonuses avoid the eye of the beholder! A single player game created by Marco Pistorio and Gaetano Chiummo and released in 2017.

214881.overview:
A horizontally scrolling western themed shooter published in Special Program N°43 (05/1988) supplement: RUN/STOP The 64 Magic Games N°1and in Hit Parade 64 N°65 (03/1992). In 2016 Hokuto Force rereleased the game with many, many fixes. Let's do a long jump into the past to reach the Old West where you will find our hero: Beppe Kid. The starting place is a fort, from this you need to reach the castle where a diamond lies. The path that leads to the castle is very dangerous, in fact, many birds of prey and some natives won't hesitate to attack you. Shoot them with your Colt, but fire sparingly because the shots are counted, or avoid the clash with the birds by jumping upward. If you reach the castle, get off your horse and venture inside the labyrinth of rooms, one of them hides the diamond. 

Collect five keys to move between floors. To access the room of the diamond you will need to compose a word formed of 6 letters, the letters are dispersed amongst the rooms. Ammo is scarce, so conserve as much as possible. You may find some in the castle if you are lucky. The game ends when you return the diamond to the fortress.

214886.overview: A single player SEUCK based shooter from Jan Maly and Peter Siekmann, published in 2002. Big Momma. She rules the world, the forbade sex, fight her and make us sexually free again. You are our last hope! Version 1.1 has music, while earlier versions did not.

214887.overview: A one or two player, SEUCK based shooter from Jan Maly and Peter Siekmann, released just like the original in 2002 with a similar theme and goal. Sexual freedom in shooter form.

214909.overview:
An action dance game put out by Edizione Logica 2000/Logica 2000 and published in Edizione Logica 2000 Supplementi #04 - Speciale n.01 - Squinzie, and also in Sfitinzie & Paninari 64 compilation. 

It would later be unofficially translated in 2017 and subtitled Metalheads vs MadonnaGirls dance challenge.

214910.overview: To clear rows, form binary numbers that match the decimals on the right. Based on Emacs Bintris. The rows are binary numbers where each block represents a 1 and an empty place represents a zero. Match the numbers on the right and the row will clear. Match multiple lines for potential BinTetris!

214911.overview: Blok Copy is a puzzle game. The player is at presented with a 5x7 board consisting of different kinds of tiles. At the start each column has only one kind of tile but the tiles will then get shuffled around. The aim of the game is then to restore the board as it was at the start. The player uses the keyboard to move the rows and columns until the board has been restored. Once completed another board will be unlocked. There are ten in total. The time is limited so the player can't take too long.

214912.overview: Bombakereső - A new MineSweeper for the C64!  I'm sure many of you have heard of MineSweeper; a puzzle game in which players had to clear the board of numbers without coming across deadly exploding bombs, using help from clues about the number of neighbouring mines in each field. But I bet you haven't heard of Bombakereső, which is the latest C64 game to be developed by Krissz! It features a definable play size and difficulty levels and a space theme to make it nicely atmosphereic.

214913.overview:
A German language text adventure with Hi-Res Graphics created by Andreas Mettler in 1986. Loosely inspired by the Scrooge McDuck comics.
Written in 1986, but forgotten by the author until 2016.

214914.overview:
An updated version of the original Bounder game, with a few bugs fixed (but retaining the cheat modes of the original). Like the original you control a tennis ball that constantly bounces on the screen. The player has to move the ball around between two bounces so it lands on friendly areas like grass or the main hexagonal-patterned floor. If it lands on hazardous areas like spikes and sand, or hits the enemies which move around, one of the seven lives the player starts with is lost. There are beneficial squares though - arrows which keep the ball in the air longer or teleports which clear part of the game. 
 
This was officially released by Gremlin in the 10 Great Games compilation.

216002.overview: In a surprising turn of events, Jack has to climb the beanstalk gathering stuff before the excavator destroys said stalk.

217562.overview: A compilation of 1987's finest Boulder Dash work by The Blockheads of the Netherlands including Boulder Dash 24,27 & Boulder Head 4,5,6 + all in one D64 image for the Commodore 64. Compilation compiled by Woodstock with release in 2021.

217640.overview:
Blow Out is a miscellaneous shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Bob Root using Garry Kitchen's GameMaker. The year of release is unknown.

You control a tank that starts on the bottom of the screen. There are several sections which enemies cross. Your goal is to wipe out as many enemies as you can without losing all your lives. Be careful, because as the game progresses, the enemies speed up. 

The enemies themselves do not shoot you, instead they kill you by running you down.

218167.overview:
This game is a tribute to Bagman, an arcade game released by Valadon Automation in 1982. It is also the sequel to Bagman Comes Back.

This version is made up of 24 completely new stages.

The game works perfectly on both PAL and NTSC models. However, for game speeds similar to the original arcade game, it is suggested using an NTSC model.

Gameplay
The objective of the game is to maneuver the bagman through various mine shafts, picking up money bags and placing them in a wheelbarrow at the surface of the mine. The player must avoid pursuing guards, moving ore carts, and descending elevators. The player can temporarily stun the guards by striking them with a pickaxe or by dropping a money bag on them when they are below the player on the same ladder, or by sliding a bag on them when they are further down the same slope. The guards can also be stunned by placing the wheelbarrow at the top of the ladder or elevator while they are going up. The pickaxes can also be used to break down walls that obstruct the passage. Keep in mind that bagman can hold the same pickaxe for a few seconds, after which it disappears. The initial duration of each pickaxe is 8 seconds, but if the player drops a pickaxe before it expires and then picks it up again, the duration resets to 4 seconds each time. Bagman can jump into an ore cart after grabbing a ceiling handle as well as he can jump off the cart by moving the joystick left/right or by moving it up/down when the cart is on a vertical ladder.

218259.overview: This 1992 Zzap!64 release alternates between three subgames: the first a Delta-style shooter, the second a platform-shooter, and the third a puzzler in which you must guide a ball to an off-switch before the timer runs out. The game has an ending after level 8. Published in the very last Zzap!64 Megatape #37 (11/1992).

218585.overview:
Beneath the Tenement is a single-screen platformer for the Commodore 64, and the sequel to Gus Vakalis' 1991 game, The Tenement. 

This game was published in Loadstar #113.

218751.overview: Blastapede is a simple Centipede clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Tom Walker as part of the Minigame Competition 2002.

219075.overview:
You, as a lovable little amphibian, have stumbled upon the temple of Blaf. This disturbance has made you aware of the Sun god being trapped inside one of the temples, where he is kept encased in stone. While at this temple you see that it tries to destroy you with spheres on a path, so you must get firing and bust those balls before they reach the skull and end the frog's hopping life.
 
    Adventure: progress through 76 levels and 22 maps to free the sun god.
    Gauntlet: play an endless game one map with increasing difficulty
    Training: improve your skill by playing a single level

219322.overview: A SEUCK based, one or two player shoot'em up featuring cooperative play by Timoth Agar. This sequel to Timothy's original game Bio War is a big step up. Great graphics and a great playing game. Lots of thought went into making this a great playing shooter.

219324.overview: Blue Beret is a game developed by Alf Yngve using Jonathan Wells' Sideways SEUCK mod. It is a game that hopes to replicate Green Beret/Rush 'n Attack, and was released by Psytronik Software as part of "Shoot Em Up Destruction Set 3".

219325.overview: A challenging Arcade game in which you need to kill the enemies in each of the many levels by squashing them with blocks. Bootskell is an Arcade game as a clone of Pengo, which was released by Sega in 1982. The player takes on the roll of Bootskell who lives in Antarctica. The game takes place in a Labyrinth made of Ice blocks and guarded by Purple Ghosts. The aim of the game is to survive as long as possible by trying to eliminate all the ghosts throughout the 60+ levels by crushing them with Ice blocks. Just be aware they can also do the same to you!

219326.overview: Big Gun No.1 is a shooter developed by Alf Yngve using a modified version of the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit (SEUCK Redux by Richard Bayliss)  and published as part of  "Shoot Em Up Destruction Set 4" in 2017.

219665.overview: Blockie was a Tetris style game created in 1992 and published in Commodore Format 1993/10 (Issue #37), the author is currently unknown.

219669.overview:
Released At :
SEUCK Game Creation Compo 2016

An unknown Super Villain lures Bergbert, hero of the nineties, into dangerous situations, threatening to destroy the city. Bergbert returns in order to find him.

In level 1, the sewage plant spills toxic water. Shut off the valves.

In level 2, the villain turned up the generators in the power plant. Switch them off to avoid overload and citywide blackout.

In level 3, ride the conveyor belt in an ammo factory and defuse bombs, avoiding ammo test guns.

Touch objects to switch them off but be careful. Don't touch the green wastewater, the electricity from the generators or the sparks from the bombs' fuses. Detect the villain and reveal his identity.

219674.overview: BrainBreak is a tile/puzzle game for the c64 with several surprising features. It uses hires multicolour graphics and comes with 100 exciting, brain-breaking levels that can be extended by using the included editor. BrainBreak can be played on the original machine as well as using emulators.

219815.overview: Bouldercraft is a survival-oriented world simulation game based on a 2D cellular automaton. It is basically a clone of Boulder Dash with some characteristics of Minecraft (hence the name).

219863.overview:
The Bandage is a 1991 text adventure developed by Megastyle for the Commodore 64. It is heavily based on, and set in the world of The King's Quest series from Sierra. 

King Graham has died, and Rosella has to go into the forest seeking for a prince. But since she's a queen now, since her father died, the prince she will find will now be a king!. But anyway, in order to complete the game, she HAS to find him (and solve all the puzzles, and obstacles in her path (which will be very easy in this game)).

228271.overview: A Boulder Dash game created by Hartmut of Germany in Gladbeck and released as a fangame by Professor Knibble in 1988. It has 20 caves on a single level and is part of a five game set ending in Boulder Dash Heavy 05.

294842.overview: This managerial simulation for up to 4 players has the same title as the game from reLINE, but in this game you'll work as a coal miner and build up your coal empire. The game starts in 1900 and ends normally in 1933. One round in the game is like 1 month in real-time. You start with a small amount of money, buying workers and materials for your own coal miner career. You can choose from 3 difficulty levels (easy, normal, hard) and several aims in the game: Building up an predetermined cash limit or predetermined coal limit, or play any chosen amount of months. You can carry on sabotage, cause mine disasters, demoralize the mine workers and more to beat your opponents (human or computer).

375285.overview:
Battle Khaos is a 2-4 player RPG for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Rafal Kazimierski and released into the public domain in 2003.

The game was heavily inspired by the 1985 ZX Spectrum classic "Chaos: The Battle of Wizards", a game written by the legendary Julian Gallop (of X-Com fame).

375317.overview: Bat is a simple collect-em-up game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Chris T. Nadovich and released as a type-in game in the book "Commodore 64 - Fun and Games" in 1983.

379744.overview:
Be Logical is a single player puzzle game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Marc Pfadenhauer and published in the following:

-   64'er 1992/02
-   64'er 1999/06 
 
At first glance, this game by Marc Pfadonouor is quite simple: all you have to do is copy the pattern that appears on the right side of the screen after the start on the left side.Unfortunately, this is associated with a problem: You cannot set the individual values ​​of a stone directly, you can only influence it through the neighboring stone. Be Logical unzips and displays the status bar and two play fields. In the status line you can see the last game status reached (of course 0 after loading). After pressing the fire button on joystick 2, this status line switches. Now the time in which you have to complete this level will be counted down. The current score, the current level and the number of lives are continuously displayed at the top of the screen. 

Move the cursor in your (left) field with the joystick in port 2. The cursor follows on the right field. In this way, you retain clarity with complicated patterns. With the fire button you place a star with the value 1 in your playing field. The value of such a stone cannot be increased if you place a stone on this position a second time. If place a 7wide stone immediately above or below this. The new stone also has the value 1. The previously placed stone then has the value 2. 

Use the space bar to determine the direction in which other stones will be affected. The cursor in your field always indicates the direction in which other stones are being affected. If the cursor shows ropes, the stones on the left and right are increased by 1; if it points up and down, the value of these stones is increased by 1. If you made a mistake: end this round with the upper right arrow key. A life will now be deducted from you. If you want to take a break, press P. Time will stop and the playing fields will be turned off so you don't think up a strategy to solve the level during the pause If you have completed a level, the remaining time is added to the score and a new round begins.

379801.overview:
BBC Ask the Family is a 2 player only educational quiz game based on the British game show that ran from Jun 12, 1967 to October 22, 1984.

The game was developed and published by Ivan Berg Software in 1984.

402875.overview:
Bloid Bros is an unreleased 2 player co-operative side scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Paul Rogers (who also worked on the C64 versions of Double Dragon 3, Time Soldiers, and Return to Oz) 

Bloid Bros is a 2 player split screen scrolling game which was written by Paul Rogers who did Time Soldier and Double Dragon 3 on the C64.

You control two blobs which look rather like the character from Head The Ball and scroll across a basic landscape whilst shooting things. It’s nothing spectacular, but Paul mentions that it never was that great and was just merely being done in his spare time.

The game was never fully finished.

417554.overview: Four oil companies (each of which can he human or computer controlled) do battle to dominate the lucrative oil industry, buying and selling oilfields around the world. You can choose one of four main goals, from topping the market in 3 years to total domination. Plenty of dirty tricks to help you are on offer, from setting fire to opponent's rigs to stealing the storage tanks which hold the oil in place. Private investigators can be hired to either prevent to prove these things. Although primarily a strategy game, a few short action sequences are also included. These come into play when attempting to drill for oil (you can hire a specialist to do this instead, but the cost is prohibitive in the early stages), to build oil pipelines around those of your opponents, and to extinguish any fires opponents start on your rig.

417862.overview: The classic Worm\Snake game. You must eat to survive, but eating makes you grow longer, which in turn increases the chance you will bite your own tail and end the game. This one was released to PD as part of the 4k BASIC Compo 2009 and was created by Colt Seavers.

417864.overview: A SEUCK shooter created by Roberto Ricioppo and released in 2012.  A simple SEUCK game in which you shoot a dart gun at the safari animals to tranquilize them (so that they can be put back safely in to their own homes).

417875.overview: You, a sentient soap bubble, have been arrested for your political beliefs by the ruling class of your society, an ancient race of dragons. You find yourself imprisoned in a maze-like dungeon from which you must escape. There is but a single exit, and it will require five different keys to open. You will find these keys randomly deposited throughout the dungeon, but each room presents its own hazards: moving walls, fireballs, hovering sentry robots, and dragon officials. Being a soap bubble, you must be very careful to avoid touching any of these hazards, and the dungeon walls as well, otherwise you will pop. Fortunately, bubbles, like cats, have nine lives.

417883.overview:
A SEUCK game by Anthony Burns in conjunction with The New Dimension for one or two players, with cooperative play available. NOTE: This game contains nudity and situations that some may found offensive. This is to some degree a one-player game, but it uses both joysticks, so two player is naturally easier. You start the game on foot, using joystick port two (If you try to start using port one, you will not be able to progress beyond the opening screen). If you can get past level 2, you will be instructed to switch to port one. From this point on, you will be flying, and the game will scroll automatically.

When you are told to “stand by” do not move the joystick, or you risk colliding with dangerous areas of the background. These have been placed in such a way as to make certain levels inaccessible to the “walker” and others to the “flyer” so that they can only be on-screen at the correct time.

When you are on-foot, you fight at close range, in the direction you are pointing. Do not venture off the grey walkways: the infrastructure of the conversion centre is deadly to the touch, and keep clear of the walkway edges where the passage is narrow. Similar caution applies when you are flying: steer clear of anything that is not plain sky (unless it is a bonus pickup). When you are flying, you fire forwards, with a long-range weapon.

417939.overview: An arcade style game from Emir Akaydin and Kursad Karamahmutoglu released as part of the Game Over(view) Freestyle Jam.

417941.overview: An action\arcade style game from Zerozillion and released to PD at the 2nd 4k BASIC Compo in 2009.

417942.overview: A logic\puzzle game created by Charles Grey and released as part of the Minigame Competition 2008 - 1K Category. Block Fill is a simple puzzle game: you're facing an 8x8 playing field made of 64 squares. Some squares are solid, some are empty. Your goal is to make all the squares solid.
